matchstick.title: V↔X transformation via single stick reposition
matchstick.principle: A V (two diagonal sticks) can be turned into an X (two crossing diagonals) by moving one diagonal stick, changing its value by ±5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a V or X appears and a value change of 5 is needed.
matchstick.example: V → X (5 → 10) by moving one diagonal to cross the other.

matchstick.title: Check numeric discrepancy to guide stick moves
matchstick.principle: Compute the integer values of both sides; the difference tells how much the total must increase or decrease.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before trying any move, calculate the numeric mismatch between the two sides.
matchstick.example: If left side is 4 and right side 11, you need to reduce the RHS by 7.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign integrity
matchstick.principle: The ‘=’ sign must remain exactly two horizontal sticks; it cannot be altered or used as a source or destination for sticks.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick move is considered; never move sticks from or to the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Do not take a horizontal stick from ‘=’ to form a minus sign.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting characters after move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, each numeral and operator must still be a recognizable Roman numeral or a valid operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each candidate move, check that every character remains valid.
matchstick.example: Turning ‘+’ into ‘-’ is valid; turning ‘V’ into a single diagonal is invalid.

matchstick.title: Avoid orientation mismatches
matchstick.principle: Sticks retain their orientation; a vertical stick cannot become diagonal, and a horizontal cannot become vertical.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a stick, ensure the destination requires the same orientation.
matchstick.example: A diagonal stick can only be placed where a diagonal is needed (e.g., V↔X).

matchstick.title: Operator conversion only when resulting operator is valid
matchstick.principle: Changing an operator (e.g., ‘+’ to ‘-’) must leave both the original and the new operator as valid symbols.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from ‘+’ yields ‘-’, which is a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Recompute numeric values after transformation
matchstick.principle: After any stick move, recalculate the Roman‑numeral values to verify that the equality now holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After proposing a move, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: After turning ‘VII’ into ‘VIII’ and ‘+’ into ‘-’, recompute 8 − 4 = 4.

matchstick.title: Plus‑to‑minus conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; moving the vertical stick away turns it into a minus sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a reduction of the RHS is needed and a vertical stick is available from the plus sign.
matchstick.example: ‘+’ → ‘-’ by moving its vertical stick elsewhere.

matchstick.title: Dual‑character stick relocation for balancing values
matchstick.principle: Moving a stick from one character to another simultaneously changes both characters’ values; use this to offset the numeric discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a single stick can both reduce one side and increase the other to achieve equality.
matchstick.example: Move the vertical stick from ‘+’ to ‘VII’, turning ‘+’ into ‘-’ and ‘VII’ into ‘VIII’.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick addition creates extra I (value +1)
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a numeral can form a new I character, increasing the numeral’s value by 1 for each added I.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a small increase (by 1) is needed and a vertical stick is available to be moved.
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical stick to ‘VII’ yields ‘VIII’ (7 → 8).

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats sticks as interchangeable symbols rather than fixed‑orientation segments.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Remember that a vertical stick stays vertical, a diagonal stays diagonal, and a horizontal stays horizontal when moved.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may think any stick can be taken from any character to balance values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never move sticks from or to the ‘=’ sign; it must remain two horizontal bars.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid character after move
matchstick.why_it_happens: Removing a stick can leave a shape that does not correspond to any Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, verify that every character still matches a known numeral or operator.

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may relocate a stick from an operator without checking the resulting symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure any operator transformation results in a valid operator (e.g., ‘+’ → ‘-’, not a stray line).

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tries random stick moves without first understanding how the values differ.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Compute the numeric difference between sides first; use it to guide the direction and magnitude of the needed change.
